key_insight: QuTOP replaces device-first, iterative quantum compiler tuning with top-down selection guided by reusable rules and learned predictors.
engineering_relevance: Jointly considering hardware targets and compiler settings can avoid backend choices that limit execution fidelity while reducing online selection latency.
method: Build QuOPTBench by exhaustively searching configurations for 268 quantum circuits.
Use an LLM to extract transferable configuration-selection rules from sampled circuits.
Combine those rules with predictors trained on enumerated configuration data to select configurations without iterative online search.
evidence_signal: Across evaluations including ten representative LLMs, vanilla LLMs remained far from oracle performance, distilled rules improved LLM selection, and QuTOP achieved the strongest overall quality–latency balance among tested baselines.
watch_item: Transfer to unseen circuit families or changing hardware calibrations needs validation, and exhaustive offline search may become costly as configuration spaces grow.
paper_title: Turning Quantum Compiler Configuration Selection Upside Down: A Top-Down Paradigm
